findings.reason: Verified: V2 canView() is canViewClientDefault() || hasPermission(VIEW) with no MANAGE check, while canManage() accepts all-clients MANAGE, and ClientsResource.getClients calls requireList(), which falls through to canView(), so an all-clients MANAGE holder is refused the client list; the PR's own testManageAllClients and testManageOnlyOneClient expect that listing to succeed.

Verified: getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources without setType, so findByType("Clients") only matches the all-clients type resource, which yields the literal name "Clients" and never per-client grants; the caller AvailableRoleMappingResource.java:229 relies on this set.

The orphaned-resource gap predates this PR, since V2 never cleaned up client resources before either, and the claim that the guard skips the listener is only true when V1 is off; with both flags on the listener runs and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws, which the finding misses.

Verified in ClientPermissionsV2.java: the logger field, the Scope import, the TOKEN_EXCHANGE import and the private getEvaluationContext (with its ClientModelIdentity, DefaultEvaluationContext and EvaluationContext imports) are unused, so this is correct but only a cleanup.
Correct that the void requireView() and requireViewClientScopes() Javadoc says "Returns true", but this is a documentation wording issue only.
